raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-UK-FreeBreakfastClubs",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Delay or failure in passing the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill could compromise the statutory mandate requiring primary schools to provide free breakfast clubs.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Engage closely with parliamentary stakeholders to track legislative progress and provide preliminary non-statutory guidance for voluntary school adoption.",
      "evidence": "Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state-funded schools with primary-aged children to offer a free breakfast club"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Primary schools may lack sufficient physical dining or kitchen space to accommodate mandatory breakfast club provision for all pupils on roll.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Deploy technical estate advisers to evaluate school premises and advise on spatial reconfiguration and flexible delivery options.",
      "evidence": "...continuing contracts of technical estate advisers to test what schools can do to mitigate any space constraints."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Delays in developing the internal CRM minimum-viable product by November 2025 could disrupt the Cohort 1 expression of interest process and onboarding support.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement agile development sprints with dedicated internal resources and prepare fallback manual onboarding workflows.",
      "evidence": "...develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum-viable product from November 2025."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Simplified funding rates (£25 daily plus £1 per pupil) may fail to cover costs for schools facing high food inflation or non-standard staffing ratios.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Monitor early rollout expenditure data closely and provide Section 14 grant adjustments or guidance on efficient food procurement.",
      "evidence": "Schools delivering their offer in-house, keeping food costs low, and staffing broadly in line with standard ratios were generally able to operate..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Closure of the National School Breakfast Programme in July 2026 could leave participating schools with a gap in provision before Cohort 2 starts in September 2026.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Guarantee transition places for all current NSBP schools and streamline early application and grant transfer processes.",
      "evidence": "...ensure they do not have a gap in provision after the closure of the NSBP in July 2026."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "School leaders may be reluctant to participate in rollout cohorts due to administrative burdens or concerns over delivery complexity.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Simplify funding structures, provide £1,000 upfront start-up grants, and offer first-line support materials to minimize friction.",
      "evidence": "...potentially increase willingness to engage and join the programme."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Delays or reductions in budget approvals from HM Treasury for future years could destabilize national rollout expansion beyond Year 1.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Submit robust business case updates early, supported by early adopter and Year 1 evaluation findings, to secure timely settlement approvals.",
      "evidence": "The programme's success depends on several factors. These include timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Shortages of qualified supervisory and catering personnel across the education sector could hinder schools' ability to staff clubs safely.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Issue flexible staffing model guidance to schools and coordinate with sector partners to assist in recruitment planning.",
      "evidence": "...availability of skilled staff and resources, in both DfE and the education sector."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Special schools and alternative provision settings may face complex operational challenges that standard mainstream support structures do not address.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Procure specialized advisers through the educational framework and maintain tailored funding rates for special settings.",
      "evidence": "To support schools with more complex delivery challenges, we launched a procurement process to increase the number of advisers..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Schools may fail to comply with statutory school food standards due to catering limitations or cost pressures.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide clear nutritional templates and pre-approved compliant menu options during onboarding, backed by compliance monitoring.",
      "evidence": "Food provided must be in line with school food standards."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Delays in commercial procurement for the call-centre pilot could lead to gaps in data collection and operational oversight.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Fast-track procurement timelines and establish interim online data submission channels for participating schools.",
      "evidence": "We will also start commercial processes to begin a call-centre pilot to support data collection."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Relying on only one term of Early Adopter scheme findings may obscure unforeseen long-term delivery issues when scaling to 2,000 schools.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement an iterative mixed-methods evaluation plan running from 2026 to 2028 to capture emerging operational lessons.",
      "evidence": "...at the point of writing, this business case had one term's worth of learning."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Uneven capacity or engagement among local authorities could lead to inconsistent implementation support across different geographic regions.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide dedicated local authority grant funding alongside clear guidance toolkits to standardize delivery expectations.",
      "evidence": "...fund local authorities to support schools and the wider system to effectively deliver free breakfast clubs."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Fluctuations in daily pupil attendance could cause unpredictable funding allocations for schools under the £1 per child model.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Maintain the guaranteed £25 daily fixed base rate and £1,000 start-up grant to ensure financial stability against variable attendance.",
      "evidence": "...there will always be a level of uncertainty at an individual school level and on a day-to-day basis."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Upfront expansion costs without immediate short-term educational attainment gains could prompt value-for-money criticisms during early rollout.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Highlight immediate labor-market and household savings benefits while communicating the multi-year timeline for educational attainment returns.",
      "evidence": "...costs are incurred upfront while attainment benefits only materialise after at least one year."
    }
  ]
}
